purpose: This page tells the story behind the practice in the founder's own words: why it started, how it grew, and how patients find it. It gives a patient a person to trust, and it repeats the rules the whole site keeps: care at home, a physician who reviews every plan, and the price in writing.
owner_notes: It is a trust page, not a sales page. It restates what the rest of the site keeps to: a physician reviews every plan, the price is in writing first, and no result is promised.
The part called How we meet patients says most people are sent by a chiropractor, a physical therapist or a family doctor. That matches the private pages for patients sent by a provider.
It names the care coordinator who sets up the video call, by first name, as the Booking page does.
A shorter founder block on the Our team page links here.
replace: Your founder's name, title and portrait go at the top of the page.
Your own four figures go under the opening: patients cared for, licensed clinicians, states served and the year founded.
Your founder's short quote and three-paragraph origin story go under The origin story, in the founder's words.
Your own four milestones go in the timeline, with your years and events.
Your care coordinator's first name goes in How we meet patients.
keep: The line in the origin story that the practice does not promise results.
The line that if this is not a fit, the practice says so and tells the patient who to see next.
The promise that the price goes in writing before the patient decides.
The small print at the foot of the page: statements not evaluated by the FDA, individual results vary.

top.say: This is the opening of the Our founder page, with the founder's name and the practice's idea in one sentence; the name on this example is a sample.

numbers.say: These are four figures about the practice; on this example they are sample figures.

why-exists.say: This is the origin story in the founder's own words, opening with a short quote; on this example it is fictional.

milestones.say: This is a short timeline of how the practice took shape; the years and events on this example are fictional.

how-we-meet-patients.say: This part says how patients usually find the practice and what the first step is.

questions.q: What is the Our founder page for?
alt: Why is there a page just for the founder?
questions.say: It tells a patient why your practice exists, in your founder's own words. It has a short origin story, a timeline of milestones, and a note on how patients find you. It gives people a person to trust before they book.

alt: How does a patient find the founder page?
questions.say: Open the menu at the top, choose About, then Our founder. The story is a little way down, under the heading The origin story, in the founder's words. The Our team page also links to it.

questions.q: What do I replace on the Our founder page?
alt: What do you need from me for the founder page?
What do I change on this page?
questions.say: Your founder's name and title, a short quote, and the origin story in three short paragraphs. Then your own milestones and your own figures. Everything on this example, including {{site.founder.name}}, is a sample.

alt: Is Dr. Demo a real person?
questions.say: No. {{site.founder.name}} is a fictional founder, and the story, the years and the milestones are samples. On your own site this page carries your founder's story.

questions.q: What has to stay in the founder's story?
alt: Can I rewrite the founder story any way I like?
Can the founder story say our treatment works?
questions.say: You tell it in your own words, but its honest lines stay. The price goes in writing before a patient decides. You do not promise results, and if someone is not a fit, you say so.

questions.q: What does the founder page say about how patients find us?
alt: Does the founder page mention the providers who send me patients?
questions.say: On this example it says most people hear about the practice from someone they trust, such as a chiropractor, a physical therapist or a family doctor. The first step is the same for everyone: a video call with a clinician. That text is a sample you replace with your own.

alt: What's the story behind this practice?
questions.say: On this example, the founder says people drove a long way and went home without a clear answer or a clear price. So a nurse practitioner comes to your home, and a physician reviews your plan first. The founder and the story are samples.

questions.q: What's the first step if I want to go ahead?
alt: Who do I talk to first?
questions.say: The page says the first step is the same for everyone: a video call with a clinician. On this example {{site.coordinator.first}}, the {{site.coordinator.role}}, sets it up; that name is a sample. You get the steps and the price in writing, and time to think it over.
